claims.statement: Tom Allen was holder of the American championship when Jem Mace was matched with him, in 1869.
claims.excerpt: was matched with Tom Allen, holder of the American championship

claims.statement: Jem Mace beat Tom Allen by knockout in ten rounds at Kennerville, Louisiana, on May 10, 1870, for the world heavyweight championship.
claims.excerpt: They met at Kennerville, May 10, 1870, world’s heavyweight championship.

claims.statement: Joe Goss beat Tom Allen on a foul in 1876, when only Allen's American title was at stake.
claims.excerpt: when Allen and Goss battled in 1876 the former had but one title, that of America, to risk.

quotes.speaker: Charles F. Mathison
quotes.text: Mace won by knockout in ten. rounds, so that when Allen and Goss battled in 1876 the former had but one title, that of America, to risk.
quotes.topic: Allen's title at the time of his 1876 fight with Goss

fights.excerpt: They met at Kennerville, May 10, 1870, world’s heavyweight championship.
fights.notes: Described in Charles F. Mathison's 1928 letter. Mace won by knockout.

fights.excerpt: when Allen and Goss battled in 1876 the former had but one title, that of America, to risk.
fights.notes: Lost on a foul, per Mathison's letter. No place or day given.

notes: A 1928 Runyon column about the world heavyweight title. Tom Allen appears only in Mathison's letter; other items (Heeney, Tunney, baseball) are not recorded.
